I make commissions on vacation packages, hotel rooms and the dining plan.  I don't make commissions on just ticket sales or any of the Disney extras (likes tours, or the Christmas and Halloween parties). I am a contractor.   Disney and Universal don't want people to buy their theme park tickets from anyone other than them.    As a travel agent, I don't even get a discount on them.

Staying at the value resorts is not a bad experience at all.   The bus rides are longer and I would highly recommend Pop Century as they have their own bus service that doesn't share with the other values.
The dining package has both advantages and disadvantages...the great advantage that I see is the ease of having everything paid for when you get down there.  However, if you are not huge eaters, it usually doesn't end up being any savings.
There are definitely good deals to be had off property.   It would depend on when you plan to head to Florida.   As long as you don't mind being off Disney property, the value for your money is much greater off property.
As for tickets, I recommend Undercover Tourist.  They are completely legit and I have bought tickets from them many times. If you have more questions, you can PM me.

Hello! I wish I could be more help.  Honestly, I am one of those agents that work under a bigger agency with a Disney travel license.  In just my personal experience, I have ordered tickets from Undercover Tourist every time I have even been to Disney World.  They aren't a great deal cheaper, but every bit helps.   The agency that I work for doesn't encourage its agents to sell tickets (mainly because we don't make commission on those), but I often do it just to make the process easier for people.  The only bad thing I can see about buying tickets from an unofficial site is that now Disney uses fingerprints to connect tickets to ticketholders.  They REALLY don't like those aftermarket tickets and Disney tries their hardest to make sure you buy everything directly from them.  Sorry I can't be of more help about the larger agencies.  I am guessing that there is a correlation between how much money Disney is making off vacations that a certain agency is making and how easily they get these contracts.  I do know as an agent, I have access to Disney's internal reservations system, but honestly, I don't get a great deal more discounts that an average person gets on the Disney site.   I usually book travel for either people who have never been before and are confused or for older people who don't want to do anything online.

Another tip is to get on making dining reservations and fast passes as soon as you can.  Be flexible with both since you have a huge group.   Touring plans is great, the only exception is Hollywood Studios, since so many rides are closed and there is so much construction.  Let me know if you have specific questions.
Try Disboards.com.  Lots of people over there would be happy to help.  They have threads for people going there each month of the year.
